name: erewhon
author: grids-agent
description: HARD. Conway's Game of Life, run backwards. The clue is a 6x6 grid ('#' alive, '.' dead, rows newline-joined) that is the state AFTER one Life step on a 6x6 board with dead cells outside. The answer is any 6x6 grid that steps to it (a predecessor / 'Garden of Eden' hunt). The scorer applies one Life step to the submitted grid and compares to the clue, counting the 8 neighbours as flat-string offsets around i (newlines count as dead cells, so rows cannot wrap). Non-'.#' characters are treated as dead, which is harmless. The generator rerolls any target that is a still life, so echoing the clue back does not score. Discovery path: the name is 'nowhere' backwards, and the answer has exactly the same shape as the clue - so 'apply some cellular rule to my grid and compare' is guessable, and Life is the overwhelmingly likely rule. The hard part is that the obvious direction is wrong: stepping the clue FORWARD scores 0, you have to invert. Expected route: try clue-as-answer (0), try step(clue) (0), then realise from the demo that step(solution) == clue. Implementation is a row-by-row DP over the 64 possible 6-bit rows (a few thousand transitions), or a randomised search. Rated hard on both discovery and implementation.
